hints: Focus on what is actually a gas at room conditions, water will be liquid here, not steam.
Write the balanced equation for propan-1-ol, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O} + 4.5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and work out the oxygen needed for 0.100 mol.
Add together the volume of $\text{CO}_2$ formed plus the volume of leftover $\text{O}_2$, remembering $1$ mol of gas is $24.0 \text{dm}^3$ at room conditions.
walkthrough:
**Write the balanced combustion equation**

Start by getting the chemistry right. Propan-1-ol is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O} + 4.5\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find oxygen used and oxygen left over**

One mole of fuel needs 4.5 moles of $\text{O}_2$, so 0.100 mol needs $0.100 \times 4.5 = 0.450$ mol.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$V = n \times 24.0 \text{ dm}^3 \text{ mol}^{-1}$$
Volume needed $= 0.450 \times 24.0 = 10.8 \text{ dm}^3$. You started with $12.0 \text{ dm}^3$, so excess $\text{O}_2 = 12.0 - 10.8 = 1.20 \text{ dm}^3$. This excess stays as gas.

**Find the volume of gaseous product**

At room conditions, water is liquid, so it contributes no gas volume. Only $\text{CO}_2$ counts.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$n(\text{CO}_2) = 0.100 \times 3 = 0.300 \text{ mol}$$
Volume $\text{CO}_2 = 0.300 \times 24.0 = 7.20 \text{ dm}^3$.

**Add up the final gas volume**

Final gas is product gas plus leftover reactant gas.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$V_{final} = V(\text{CO}_2) + V(excess \text{ O}_2) = 7.20 + 1.20 = 8.40 \text{ dm}^3$$

options.A: This is only the volume of $\text{CO}_2$ formed ($0.300$ mol $\times$ $24.0 = 7.20 \text{dm}^3$). It forgets that oxygen was in excess, so the $1.20 \text{dm}^3$ of unused $\text{O}_2$ must also be counted in the final gas.
options.B: Correct. $\text{CO}_2$ formed is $7.20 \text{dm}^3$ and excess $\text{O}_2$ is $1.20 \text{dm}^3$. Water is liquid at room conditions so is not included. Total $= 7.20 + 1.20 = 8.40 \text{dm}^3$.
options.C: This wrongly counts water as a gas. $0.400$ mol of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ would be $9.60 \text{dm}^3$ as gas, plus $7.20 \text{dm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$ gives $16.80 \text{dm}^3$. At room conditions water condenses to liquid, so it must be excluded.
options.D: This counts everything as gas: $\text{CO}_2$ ($7.20$) + gaseous $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($9.60$) + excess $\text{O}_2$ ($1.20$) $= 18.00 \text{dm}^3$. The trap is treating water as a gas at room conditions when it is actually liquid.
